subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 28-year-old man with a mild mitochondrial myopathy undergoes metabolic testing. He has exercise intolerance and mild lactic acidosis, and his muscle biopsy shows ragged red fibers. In isolated mitochondria with an intact electron transport chain, oxidation of acetyl-CoA is measured.
question: Complete oxidation of one acetyl-CoA molecule in the TCA cycle and electron transport chain yields approximately how many ATP equivalents?
explanation_correct: One turn of the TCA cycle produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 GTP; using 2.5 ATP per NADH and 1.5 ATP per FADH2, this equals 7.5 plus 1.5 plus 1, or about 10 ATP per acetyl-CoA. Because one glucose yields two acetyl-CoA, the TCA cycle contributes about 20 ATP per glucose.

explanation_incorrect.A: Two ATP equivalents is the net yield of anaerobic glycolysis per glucose; acetyl-CoA oxidation yields considerably more.
explanation_incorrect.B: Five ATP equivalents would be produced by two NADH molecules, not by the full oxidation of one acetyl-CoA.
explanation_incorrect.C: 7.5 ATP corresponds only to the three NADH molecules produced per turn of the cycle and ignores the FADH2 and GTP.
explanation_incorrect.D: Nine ATP accounts for the NADH and FADH2 but omits the GTP generated by substrate-level phosphorylation.

educationalObjective: Each acetyl-CoA oxidized in the TCA cycle yields 10 ATP equivalents: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 GTP.
